Riley, thanks — this is clear and a great kickoff list. High level answers below and a proposed timeline. I'll follow up with a short MAP doc you can iterate on.

Quick answers / asks:
- API keys & service account: we can provision a scoped service account for the evaluation. Keys are ephemeral by default (7-day rotation); we can shorten if you need more frequent rotation. Please confirm the admin email for org ownership and whether you want SCIM enabled.
- Org setup: recommend one org owner admin; Redwood will send an invite to that email and provide the SCIM provisioning endpoint if you enable it.
- IP allowlist: Redwood can publish a small set of egress IPs for our hosted endpoints. For VPC peering we can provide the peer subnet ranges once we confirm region.
- VPC peering workflow: standard flow — 1) you open a peering request, 2) we accept, 3) exchange route tables and test. We'll provide a sample AWS route table snippet.

Proposed short schedule (2-week sprint):
- Day 0 (kickoff): confirm org owner, provide CIDR blocks, sign MAP
- Day 2–4: API key provisioning, SCIM trial enabled, allowlist applied
- Day 5–10: VPC peering bring-up + smoke tests (KV + small load)
- Day 11–14: acceptance window + quick evaluation report

Next steps: I'll attach a Redwood MAP template and drop a draft schedule in the thread. Can you confirm the org owner email and the CIDR ranges this week?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Looping in technical acceptance criteria so Novara can validate once the environment is up. Inline notes below.

> - API key provisioning, SCIM trial enabled, allowlist applied

Notes / TAC (technical acceptance criteria):
1) API keys: token lifecycle documented, ability to rotate without downtime (we use rolling keys). Expected test: rotate keys during smoke test and confirm no 500s in a 5-min window.
2) Auth: SCIM provisioning acceptable; if you prefer SAML we need SAML metadata.
3) Network: once we have your CIDRs, Redwood will provide the endpoint IP block (two /28s per region). Test: curl to the inference endpoint from a bastion within your network to confirm TLS and response headers.
4) VPC peering: planning table — we require a peering CIDR that does not overlap, mutual route update, and testing plan (ping, curl, tokenized request).
5) Performance baseline: for evaluation we'll configure a conservative throughput target (10 rps, 1k tokens/session). If you want higher throughput, we must reserve dedicated capacity which impacts cost.

I'll attach a one-page acceptance checklist you can use for signoff.

-Ben
Ben Carter
SRE / Solutions
Redwood Inference
